analyst.summary: Indian Hotels (Taj) just delivered its best-ever year - record revenue, margins and profit, a net-cash balance sheet with an AAA+ rating, and a fast-diversifying new-businesses arm (Ginger, Qmin, Tree of Life) growing well ahead of the core hotel business. The catch is the price: the stock trades at roughly 1.5-2x the PE multiple of listed peers like EIH and Chalet Hotels, occupancy is already near a cyclical high leaving less room for further gains, management has itself guided FY27 growth down a notch (12-14% versus FY26's 16%), and the West Asia conflict is currently denting the international portfolio. We rate this a Hold: a genuinely well-run business, but one priced for a level of continued perfection that leaves little cushion if growth merely meets rather than beats guidance.
